dimensions.note: No credential or secret handling. denoBin is an executable name or path, not a secret, and resolveDenoBin falls back to DENO_BIN before the ~/.swamp/deno/deno path so nothing has to be vaulted.

checkScaffolding logs a structured completion line and a warn when deno is missing, but nothing on entry, so a run that finds no scaffolding dirs is silent apart from the completion line. This matches the pre-existing pattern in this extension (checkExtensions, checkGitignore, findHardcodedPaths also log only on completion), so it is a file-wide follow-up rather than a regression from this change.

A missing deno executable is a reported skip with an actionable skipReason, not an exception. A non-zero deno check whose output cannot be parsed becomes a file-level error finding carrying the last three stderr lines, so a deno output-format change degrades to a visible finding instead of silent success. The one gap: resolveDenoBin probes candidates with --version and swallows probe failures, so a deno binary that resolves but then fails to spawn inside runDenoCheck would surface as a raw Deno.Command throw.

Six new tests cover the pure helpers (stripAnsi, isScaffoldingSource, parseDenoCheckOutput x4 including ANSI, hint lines, location-less output, clean runs and percent-encoded URLs), bringing the extension to 17. The checkScaffolding IO path itself is untested: dir walking, nearestPackageRoot resolution, resolveDenoBin fallback order, and the deno invocation. Consistent with this extension's existing pure-helper-only test style. The parser was separately verified end-to-end against real `deno check .pi/extensions/swamp-audit.ts` output during this review: 5 diagnostics parsed, all 5 with correct file and line.
Read-only: it typechecks files and writes one resource. Re-runnable, no external mutation, no partial-write window because the resource is written once from a fully assembled report.

Parses `deno check` human-readable diagnostics — an undocumented format — after stripping ANSI codes, pairing each `TS<code> [ERROR|WARN]` header with the next `at file://...` location. Rendered to real output during review. Note that `deno check` resolves the scaffolding's declared jsr:/npm: imports, so a scheduled run performs implicit network fetches for whatever those plugins import; that is inherent to typechecking, not a defect here.

The single Deno.Command is awaited via output(), so stdout/stderr pipes are drained and closed by the runtime on every path. No temp files, sockets, or long-lived handles; the walk generator is fully consumed per directory.

README and test fixtures use generic roots (/repo, file:///repo/...) and repo-relative dirs; no real hostnames, home paths, IPs, or account identifiers. Default scaffoldingDirs are the generic .kilo/.opencode/.pi locations.

ScaffoldingReportSchema is a plain z.object(...) with no .passthrough(), reuses the existing FindingSchema for findings, and globalArguments is re-parsed at the top of checkScaffolding so CEL validation still works.
The new scaffolding resource declares lifetime 7d and garbageCollection 10, matching every other spec in the extension.
Not a CRUD lifecycle behavior: it audits local repo state and reports findings, with no create/update/delete/sync surface to complete.
checkScaffolding mutates nothing outside its own resource, so there is nothing to gate behind policy/live pre-flight labels.
The new spec has a single writer using the stable name scaffolding-current, distinct from scan/paths/extensions/gitignore-current. No cross-spec or cross-method collisions.
No method reads previously stored state; there is no update/delete/sync path that would need readResource.

model.version and the manifest both move to 2026.10.21.1 with a toVersion 2026.10.21.1 no-op upgrade entry, needed because globalArguments gained scaffoldingDirs and denoBin. Both new fields carry defaults, so existing instances migrate without attribute changes and the no-op entry is correct.
